content.comment_body: We need to upgrade our older [product_name] to a newer model, but want to copy the manual programming from the old device to [product_name] configuration software. The first three inputs are labeled as follows: B01 activates Q1, B02 activates Q2, and B03 activates Q3. I have attached a photo of the fourth entry: B06 activates Q4. The issue is, there are only three cables connected to the inputs (I1, I2, and I3), so it's unclear what B06 refers to, and we weren't able to get further details from the [product_name] display. This device serves as a relay for dry contacts that trigger our SNMP manager.

Manual programming using the [product_name] display hasn't been performed for several years. The information shown in your screenshot is just a portion of the current logic that manages output Q4. Block B006 is responsible for controlling Q4. You can find the [product_name] user manual here: [document]

How can I view the entire logic path that controls output Q4 (block B006)? I'm trying to understand the configuration used on these devices so I can set up the new ones without having to start from scratch.

It's not possible to display the full circuit logic on the device's display; it only shows segments at a time. The manual provides instructions for manual programming. That's why I shared the [document] link for reference.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face challenges when trying to extract or reproduce the complete logic manually programmed into older [product_name] modules. The device display only shows parts of the configuration rather than the full program, limiting a comprehensive understanding and complicating upgrades or transfers, causing uncertainty and potential installation delays.
analysis.user_expectations: Users would like to easily extract, review, and copy the entire existing logic when migrating to a newer version or updated system.
